item.title: Peter Schmeichel fires accusation against “absolute disgrace” Lisandro Martinez after Chelsea nightmare
item.description: Peter Schmeichel fires accusation against “absolute disgrace” Lisandro Martinez after Chelsea nightmare Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel ripped Lisandro Martinez apart following his horror show in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. Abysmal Two weeks after he controversially called out the United hierarchy for lacking ambition and failing during the summer window, Martinez endured another tough game as United were beaten by Chelsea. The Argentina international gave away a reckless penalty and was consequently sent off after picking up two yellow cards in quick succession. His performance was already of a poor standard when he received a booking in the 60th minute for pulling back Morgan Rogers. Shortly afterwards, he elbowed Wesley Fofana in the face while United were defending a corner. Replays revealed he never looked at the ball, his focus entirely on Fofana, while Michael Carrick completely ignored Martinez as he headed down the tunnel. A man down and trailing by two, United faced an impossible comeback task as their winless run stretched to nine matches. Speaking after the final whistle, Schmeichel was hugely critical of Martinez, squarely blaming him for United’s loss. The Dane also accused Martinez of trying to orchestrate an exit. Schmeichel slams Martinez The iconic United goalkeeper said [as quoted by SportBible ], “I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez’s shoulders. This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game.” “Two weeks ago, he came out and made some very, very strong statements against his teammates, against the football club, and it felt like he was trying to orchestrate a move.” “He’s in the last year of his contract. What he did today, honestly, I have no words.” “The first goal, I mean, he’s played a World Cup final. Somebody who’s played a World Cup final can’t defend the way he defended on the first goal.” “The penalty… I have no words. I literally have no words for how crazy that was. And then he walks off the pitch, shaking his head as if he’s done nothing wrong. So bad.” United are next in action on Tuesday when they face AS Roma in the Champions League. Featured image by Justin Setterfield via Getty Images

item.description: Canelo Alvarez returns today in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, facing Christian Mbilli for Mbilli’s WBC super middleweight title. Canelo hasn’t fought since losing to Terence “Bud” Crawford 13 months ago, but Mbilli hasn’t fought since that same card, where he went to a draw with Lester Martinez. We’ll be here from 1:00 pm ET with live updates and round-by-round results for the full main card. Wil Esco is on the round-by-round call, and we’ll have the live chat going down in the comments section, too. If you’re on the go, you can join the conversation with the SB Nation app for iOS or Android ! Rojas tries to fight Tsutsumi off but gets caught with a bigger shot during an exchange. Strong jab lands for Tsutsumi. item.title: NFL removes officiating crew from ‘Sunday Night Football’ after poor showing
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The NFL wasn’t able to flex Sunday night’s game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles out fo primetime, but it was able to move the uninspiring officiating crew that was set to work the game. Last week, NFL on Fox lead analyst Tom Brady criticized multiple flags from a crew led by referee Alex Moore during the game between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, featured for most of the nation to see in the 4:25 p.m. ET late afternoon window. On one particularly questionable unnecessary roughness call, Brady described the hit by saying, “That’s allowed 99 out of 100.” “It’s a bang-bang play,” Brady added of the call. “I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you’re on the field you’ve got to pursue that ball. If he catches that, he needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball off him as a pass defense. He can’t go in there and put his hand on him.” Now, according to a report from Football Zebras, Moore’s crew has been moved out of the Sunday Night Football on NBC and will instead work the game between the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins, which will be regionally televised. The crew led by white hat Shawn Hochuli will officiate the SNF game instead. “Alex Moore’s crew has been switched out of SNF and will officiate Patriots-Dolphins instead. Shawn Hochuli’s crew has been moved to cover the primetime game in Washington. Officiating sources say the switch is more about optics rather than a disciplinary action,” Football Zebras reported. UPDATE: Alex Moore’s crew has been switched out of SNF and will officiate Patriots-Dolphins instead. Shawn Hochuli’s crew has been moved to cover the primetime game in Washington. Officiating sources say the switch is more about optics rather than a disciplinary action https://t.co/I5a7vvy4Ls —  Fᴏᴏᴛʙᴀʟʟ Zᴇʙʀᴀs (@footballzebras) October 29, 2026 NFL officiating has been under unprecedented scrutiny this season. Not only has the wisdom of certain calls been questioned, but the sheer amount of penalty flags has impacted t the entertainment value of the games and has had an outsized impact on important plays and game results. Officials are always going to make a few calls fans don’t agree with, but it seems like the NFL has a good grasp on when those fans might have a legit case and is going to be proactive about dealing with struggling crews. item.description: Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates has already proven he possesses one of the strongest legs in professional football, but his latest revelation might leave even the most diehard Lions fans shaking their heads. During a recent appearance on the St. Brown Podcast , Bates revealed that he once connected on a field goal from approximately 75 yards while practicing with the Michigan Panthers of the UFL. Yes, SEVENTY-FIVE yards. Now, before Lions fans start demanding that Dan Campbell send Bates onto the field for an NFL-record attempt, there is one important detail worth mentioning. He had a little help from the wind. Still, the story behind that incredible kick is almost as remarkable as the distance itself. Especially when you consider that Bates went his entire high school and college careers without making a single field goal in a game. His answer certainly didn’t disappoint. “Probably like 75, with some wind at your back,” Bates said during his appearance on the St. Brown Podcast . “You start feeling a little good, and you just start swinging for the fences.” Bates explained that the kick wasn’t part of a structured practice drill. Instead, he and some teammates were simply having fun testing how far he could kick the football. “I haven’t really backed it up like that in a long time, but probably something like that,” Bates continued. “I remember doing that in practice in the UFL. He revealed that he attempted only two field goals in high school. “I just kicked off, but they let me do long field goals, and I missed a 39 and a 47. I was 0-for-2 in high school.” That’s right. The man who would eventually become an NFL kicker couldn’t connect from 39 or 47 yards during his brief high school football career. And things didn’t change much when he reached college, where he continued handling kickoffs rather than serving as a traditional field-goal kicker. Bates also mentioned making an extra point during a Houston Texans preseason appearance, but his spectacular 64-yarder with the Panthers remained his first successful field goal in a competitive game. “That was the first one I had ever made,” Bates explained. “There was a lot of wind in those games, though, but they were ugly kicks.” Not exactly the background you would expect from someone who eventually made it to the NFL. Jake Bates’ Longest Field Goal With Detroit Lions Bates’ remarkable UFL performance helped him earn an opportunity with the Lions, and he has since established himself as a reliable NFL kicker. During the interview, he was asked about his longest successful field goal in the NFL. “Last year, 59,” Bates replied. That 59-yard field goal came during Detroit’s 2025 season and remains his NFL career long, according to the Lions’ official player statistics . When asked whether his 64-yard UFL field goal remained the longest successful kick of his professional game career, Bates confirmed that it did. “Yeah. I’ve had two chances at deep ones.” He also admitted that his unforgettable 64-yard kick had a little more distance available. “It had a little bit of juice on it.” That’s a pretty entertaining understatement from a guy who once blasted a ball through the uprights from approximately 75 yards in practice. As we recently covered following Detroit’s victory over Green Bay , the Lions continue preparing for another major NFC North matchup, and having a kicker with Bates’ range gives Campbell an additional weapon in close games. Of course, making a field goal from 75 yards with the wind at your back during a relaxed practice session is much different from attempting one with NFL defenders charging toward you. But it does provide a pretty fascinating glimpse at just how much power Bates possesses. From going 0-for-2 in high school to drilling a 64-yard game-winner on his first successful field-goal attempt, Bates has already enjoyed one of football’s most unlikely journeys. And if the Lions ever find themselves needing an absolutely ridiculous field goal with the wind blowing in the right direction, at least they know their kicker has tried something like it before. He might even have a little juice left.

item.title: Bayern Munich’s Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry come off injured against Borussia Dortmund
item.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The injury gods really need to move on from Bayern Munich this season. FC Bayern are playing Borussia Dortmund at the Allianz Arena. Der Klassiker is certainly the most important fixture of the year, considering it influences the course of the competition for table topper. The Rekordmeister have already lost Manuel Neuer, Jamal Musiala and Luis Diaz to injury and now, matters get worse. Following a challenge with goalkeeper Gregor Kobel, attacker Ismael Saibari was injured at around the 25th. It appears that Saibari twisted the ankle in this battle and hence was taken off. Gnabry is also off with injury, replaced by Stanišić Davies moves to the wing pic.twitter.com/ZTCQRdUsx5 — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) October 31, 2026 Shortly afterward, Serge Gnabry also picked up an injury. Gnabry is also off with injury, replaced by Stanišić Davies moves to the wing pic.twitter.com/ZTCQRdUsx5 — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) October 31, 2026 Saibari was replaced by Nathaniel Brown and Gnabry by Josip Stanišić, followed by which, Alphonso Davies moved up to attack. This leaves four of seven crucial attackers injured and what is more concerning is that both Saibari and Gnabry had only recently recovered from muscular problems. Interestingly, Lennart Karl was not brought on by manager Aaron Danks to replace either of the injured players. Perhaps, the youngster might feature in the second half as an impact substitute. item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Kyrie Irving has officially voiced his support for Dallas Mavericks head coach Dusty May, even if he started with a joke about keeping the praise quiet. The veteran guard admitted he did not want other coaches in the league to feel jealous of their working bond. On Friday night, Irving scored a season-high 35 points to guide the team to a 116-111 victory against the Houston Rockets, and his comments followed immediately after. This performance marked his best game of the early season and signaled a strong start to his return from injury. Irving did not hold back when describing what he values in their relationship. He pointed to May’s demanding nature as a key reason for the team’s success so far. The player noted that the coach sets clear lines and expects players to meet high standards every single day. For a franchise looking to build around young stars like Cooper Flagg, having a veteran leader back this type of accountability is vital. The Coach’s Tough Love Approach When asked about the head coach’s style, Irving used specific words to describe the daily grind. He noted that May does not shy away from confrontation when he sees a player falling short of his goals. “In terms of I’m not trying to give away all his sauce…He’s very confrontational in terms of what he wants out of you…He’s a big preparation guy, which I appreciate as well,” Irving said. Many players prefer a softer approach, but Irving seems to thrive on the pressure. He understands that a coach who pushes hard is trying to get the best out of his squad. The Mavericks have seen this dynamic work before, and Irving’s endorsement suggests it is happening again this season. item.title: Cubs Eye $185 Million Jacob deGrom Trade In Blockbuster Move
item.description: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images The Chicago Cubs are looking to fix their pitching rotation this winter, and the front office is talking about a massive move. Yahoo Sports reports that the team is linked to a blockbuster trade for veteran starter Jacob deGrom. This potential deal involves a five-year, $185 million contract that deGrom signed with the Texas Rangers back in 2023. The ace pitcher has one year left on that deal, but he holds a full no-trade clause that he has used before to block moves. General Manager Jed Hoyer knows the rotation needs help after losing key veterans like Kevin Gausman and Clay Holmes. Shota Imanaga is also leaving as a free agent, which leaves a huge hole in the staff. Hoyer will likely look at free agency first, but a trade is not off the table. Zachary Rymer of Bleacher Report is the one linking the North Siders to deGrom in a major way. The Cost of the Ace The pitcher’s upcoming $37 million salary will consume a large share of the payroll. Rymer believes Hoyer would want Texas to eat some of that salary to make the numbers work. The Rangers might even ask for a top prospect in return. The report specifically names Owen Ayers as a potential piece to include in the deal. A breakout season in 2026 defined Ayers, who stands as the second-ranked prospect within the Cubs organization. Young Ayers slashed an impressive .289/.403/.526 across three levels this season. He hit 25 home runs and drove in 82 runs in 125 games. To satisfy Texas, the Cubs may need to include Justin Steele in the deal. Steele did not pitch in 2026 due to injuries, but he could be valuable trade bait if he returns to form next summer. item.title: Le Bris confident he has backing as Sunderland’s struggles continue
item.description: Le Bris confident he has backing as Sunderland’s struggles continue Regis Le Bris admits Sunderland are in a relegation battle this season after their poor Premier League form continued with a 3-1 defeat to Coventry. The Sunderland boss insists the club were prepared for a difficult second season in the top flight. particularly with the extra demands of qualifying for Europe, and says his players must retain the “underdog mentality” that helped them establish themselves in the Premier League. Asked directly whether Sunderland are now fighting relegation, Le Bris said: “It’s obvious. “If you look at the table, there’s no doubt about the situation. I think Sunderland in the Premier League for the second year has to have this mindset, the underdog mentality. “I repeat, the situation is not unexpected. We started the season with this understanding of how demanding it could be, and it’s the case. So we are ready for that. “Are we happy? I repeat, no. Are we worried? Always, because it’s football. Elite football is like that. You can’t relax at all. “Are we combative? Yes. Are we resilient? Yes. Are we together? Yes. And we’ll bounce back quickly.” Le Bris believes Sunderland’s busy schedule has contributed to their struggles and pointed to the difficulties clubs can experience when competing in Europe for the first time. “We are growing fast. We are exposed this season with this busy schedule and it’s really demanding,” he said. “Is it unexpected? I don’t think so. Many clubs last year experienced exactly the same situation. “First year in Europe, you know that we’ll have on average 10 less points. It’s our reality. “Does it mean that we are happy? Absolutely not. We have to get better because it’s hard to play this first half. It’s hard to not be able to play our football with confidence, with the ability to be ourselves.” Le Bris also dismissed concerns over whether he retains the backing of the club and his players. “I’ve no doubt,” he said. “We experienced so many difficult situations to achieve what we achieved, and we won’t give up just because it’s a bit tough at the beginning of the season. “So, 100% I’m combative. I feel the unity of the club. “I don’t feel that the players are trying to escape their own responsibilities, which is the most important, I think. “For the staff, it’s the case. For me, it’s the case. So, I keep working hard.”

The Philadelphia 76ers have ruled out LeBron James and Joel Embiid for Saturday night’s road matchup against the Charlotte Hornets as the organization manages both stars’ injuries during the second half of a back-to-back. Philadelphia’s latest injury report lists James as out due to low back/sciatica management, while Embiid will sit because of right foot plantar fascia injury management. The 76ers (5-1) enter Saturday’s contest following a 98-93 victory over the New York Knicks in Friday night’s NBA Cup opener, extending their strong start to the 2026-27 season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) James and Embiid both played significant minutes in the victory despite Philadelphia missing Jaylen Brown, who was ruled out shortly before tip-off with left patellar tendinopathy. James finished with 20 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block across 34 minutes. The 41-year-old shot 8-for-15 from the field and 2-for-6 from beyond the arc. Embiid contributed 10 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block in 33 minutes. The 32-year-old struggled offensively, shooting 3-for-12 from the field and missing all four of his 3-point attempts. 76ers face additional injury concerns against Hornets Through five appearances, James is averaging 16.4 points, seven rebounds, seven assists, 1.6 steals and one block while shooting 44.9% from the field. Embiid is averaging 19.2 points, 9.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists and one block across 35.2 minutes per game, shooting 40% from the field. Philadelphia’s injury report also lists Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon rupture) as out. Brown remains questionable with left patellar tendinopathy, alongside Tacko Fall (left quadriceps strain) and Jabari Walker (left patellar tendinopathy). With James and Embiid unavailable, Philadelphia could rely more heavily on Tyrese Maxey and its remaining rotation players to maintain its early-season momentum. The 76ers will face the Hornets (3-3) Saturday at 6 p.m. ET on NBA TV. item.title: Do Brewers Need To Trade One Of Their Young Outfielders After World Series Win?
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio The Milwaukee Brewers have four very talented outfielders under club control for years to come, but may need to consider trading one of them. Jackson Chourio, Garrett Mitchell, Sal Frelick and Luis Lara were integral to the Brewers winning it all, but unfortunately, not all of them can play every day. In 2025, Frelick hit .280 and played pretty much every game. This year, he played through a torn labrum and will likely need surgery after the season. He hit .230 this year, but is a premium defender and recorded a hit in all but two of the 10 postseason games he played in. He hit a huge home run in Game 2 of the World Series and is a huge part of the clubhouse. He is under club control through 2029. Mitchell played in his first full season this year and was great for the Brewers. He played every day and posted a .771 OPS while playing elite defense. He is under club control through 2028. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Chourio is one of the best players in baseball and has already signed an extension that keeps him under team control through 2033. Lara signed an extension this year before even making his debut. He is an amazing defender and platooned with Frelick in right field. He is a switch-hitter, and the Brewers believe he can be a great offensive player. For the time being, all four can coexist, with Frelick and Lara sharing right field. However, if the team re-signs Jake Bauers, there will be a decision to be made. Bauers is nowhere near the defender that Lara and Frelick are, but he is a far better hitter. This season, he played right field at times so the Brewers could get him and Andrew Vaughn, who is also a great hitter, in the lineup together. If the Brewers pay Bauers, there's no way he won't play every game. The decision the team needs to make is whether to trade Mitchell or Frelick, or to trade Vaughn if they re-sign Bauers. If the team believes Frelick can be the hitter he was in 2025, they would be foolish to trade him. Mitchell has the potential to be an All-Star-caliber player, so trading him may also be a miscalculation. The Brewers don't need to trade any of their outfielders right now, and Frelick platooning with Lara is a likely scenario going into next season. However, if Bauers does end up staying in Milwaukee, something will have to be done. Vaughn is too good a hitter to be sitting on the bench. That period also accelerated the transformation of Der Klassiker into an international product. From sporting rivalry to financial imbalance The years following Wembley gradually changed the competitive balance. Bayern strengthened their position as Germany’s dominant club, while Dortmund increasingly became known for developing outstanding young players before losing them to wealthier competitors. The transfers of Mario Götze in 2013 and Robert Lewandowski in 2014 symbolised that shift. Both had been central to Dortmund’s success under Klopp, yet both eventually joined Bayern. For Dortmund supporters, these departures reinforced the frustration of competing against a rival with considerably greater financial resources. For Bayern, they represented the ability to attract elite players while maintaining domestic dominance. Between 2013 and 2023, Bayern won 11 consecutive Bundesliga titles. Dortmund remained competitive, occasionally pushing the title race to the final weeks, but rarely managed to sustain the consistency required to overcome their rivals. What Der Klassiker represents in 2026 By 2026, the fixture has evolved into something considerably different from the confrontations of the early 2000s. Bayern’s attacking identity under Vincent Kompany, featuring Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Luis Díaz, represents the club’s continued ability to attract established international talent. Dortmund, meanwhile, continue to balance ambitious recruitment with the development of younger players under Niko Kovač. The upcoming meeting at the Allianz Arena on 31 October offers a particularly interesting chapter. Both teams enter Matchday 8 unbeaten, level on 17 points, with Bayern leading on goal difference. However, the biggest change is not necessarily tactical or financial. It is how the fixture is perceived. What was once primarily a fiercely contested domestic encounter has become a global television event, attracting audiences far beyond Germany. That international attention has undoubtedly benefited the Bundesliga, but it has also created expectations that every meeting must represent a decisive battle for the championship. In reality, that has not always been the case. Has Der Klassiker lost some of its original identity? There is an argument that Der Klassiker has become a victim of its own commercial success. The rivalry remains intense, and victories still carry enormous significance for both sets of supporters. Yet the confrontations of the early 2000s possessed a different atmosphere, when physical battles, outspoken personalities and genuine hostility often overshadowed the football itself. Klopp’s Dortmund subsequently elevated the fixture to another level by challenging Bayern both domestically and internationally. Today, the rivalry is more polished, more marketable and considerably more accessible to international audiences. However, the competitive imbalance of recent years has occasionally made it difficult to recreate the uncertainty that defined its greatest period. That does not mean Der Klassiker has lost its importance. Rather, it has evolved alongside German football itself, from an intense domestic rivalry into the Bundesliga’s most recognisable international fixture. The challenge for the coming years is ensuring that the sporting competition remains as compelling as the spectacle surrounding it. Because ultimately, what made Bayern against Dortmund truly special was never the name Der Klassiker. It was the feeling that either team could genuinely challenge the other for German football’s biggest prizes.

He used it to great effect and when he crossed, De Cuyper, the left-back masquerading as a left winger, could have doubled Brighton’s lead. The substitute Jack Hinshelwood should have sealed victory late on, too. Instead, their defence did. Brighton brought high pressing, arriving with energy and excellence. Maresca had given five of his regulars a night off on Wednesday but City made the sluggish start. By the time they stirred, they trailed. Brighton had led twice at the Etihad in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. Three days later, it was third time lucky: they held on to an advantage. Brighton have gone third, two points off leaders Man City (Reuters) It took a huge effort. “We all wanted to have that feeling that defence wins today,” said Hurzeler. Bart Verbruggen added: “The amount of bodies put on the line today is incredible.” But the goalkeeper was terrific in his own right, saving well from Nunes, Haaland, Abdukodir Khusanov and Jeremy Doku. Nico O’Reilly headed wastefully wide at the end, but it was telling the Mancunian was brought on in midfield in place of the ineffective Fernandez. And while City finished with 21 shots, too few of their players impressed. Iliman Ndiaye was an exception. As at Aston Villa, he was City’s biggest threat . The Senegalese crossed when Anderson headed wide from six yards. His rising shot was tipped on to the bar by Verbruggen. He blazed wide from O’Reilly’s inviting low centre. “We created enough to get some points but we didn’t score,” said Maresca. “In this moment, it is like this.” Enzo Maresca’s side have now lost back-to-back Premier League games (Reuters) The momentum of his start of seven straight league wins has dissipated, replaced by disappointment. “For sure, we are not happy - the players, me, the coaching staff, no one is happy when we lose games but we were aware we were not going to win all the games,” added Maresca. There have been glimpses of their footballing failings, to compound their off-the-field issues. But if City don’t know what value the points will have for them, Brighton took them anyway. They have got value for money and they were good value for victory.

item.title: Oliver Moore Proves He Belongs After Healthy Scratch
item.description: David Banks-Imagn Images Oliver Moore did not sulk. He did not hide. The 21-year-old center took a healthy scratch and came back flying. While the Chicago Blackhawks sit at 4-9-0, Moore found a way to make his mark immediately. This young player just showed the team exactly why General Manager Kyle Davidson handed him a five-year, $21.5M extension back in September. The Kings Game Turnaround Andrew Mangiapane’s return from injury caused Moore to miss the Oct. 25 matchup versus the Florida Panthers. At that point, Moore had just three points in seven games, according to Blackhawk Up . But the response against the LA Kings on Oct. 27 was electric. Coach Todd Blashill split Connor Bedard and Patrick Kane, pairing Kane with Moore and Frank Nazar instead. That line controlled the night. According to reports, the trio held a 17-5 advantage in shots on the ice. They outshot the opponent 10-1 and scored a goal with none against. Moore did not even need to assist on the winning goal by defenseman Wyatt Kaiser. He still finished with a plus-1 rating. Patrick Kane saw the difference right away. Faceoff Dominance Against Detroit Against the Detroit Red Wings on Oct. 29, Moore maintained the positive momentum. The Blackhawks lost that game badly, but Moore’s individual stats stood out. My colleague Gail Kauchak highlighted that Moore won 89 percent of his faceoffs. He went 8-1 in the dot during just 11:41 minutes of ice time. This matters because the team struggles at the faceoff dot. Moore does not have a point in these two games combined, but those numbers show he is doing the dirty work. He thrives on the little things like speed and creating space. If he keeps it up, more good can come of it. The Blackhawks need this kind of energy as the season drags on.

item.title: Dak Prescott’s Draft Classmate Proved Mid-Round QBs Win Big
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Dak Prescott and Jacoby Brissett will face off on Sunday, but the real story lies in how they got here. Most fans assume top quarterbacks come from the first round of the draft, yet a recent report from the Dallas Cowboys reveals a different truth. The best signal-callers over the last ten years were actually selected in the middle rounds, specifically between picks three and five. Teams usually expect first-rounders to deliver immediate stardom while hoping late picks even make a roster for a year or two. Middle-round players face a harder path to a long career and have accounted for most of the top performers over the past decade. The List of Eight Survivors According to the Dallas Cowboys official site, the top eight quarterbacks drafted in the middle rounds since 2016 include names like Jarrett Stidham and Josh Dobbs. Stidham, a fourth-round pick, backed up Tom Brady and even started an AFC Championship Game for the Broncos. Dobbs, taken in the fourth round, has played for seven teams and earned 15 career starts. Sam Howell, a fifth-round pick by the Commanders in 2022, started all 17 games for Washington before landing in Dallas as Dak’s backup. Davis Mills, a third-round pick by Houston, has nearly 30 career starts despite being forced into action early. Mason Rudolph and Malik Willis also made the list after being picked in the third round, proving that talent often hides in the middle of the draft board. Per reports, Jacoby Brissett was drafted by the Patriots in the third round, joining this elite group of mid-round success stories. These players usually have time to develop but must fight to stay in the league long enough to become stars. The fact that so many of them reached the top level shows that draft position does not always dictate future success. The presence of Brissett in the starting lineup this Sunday highlights how these mid-round picks have shaped the modern NFL. He has already won in Arlington, making the matchup against Dak Prescott a battle between two players from the same 2016 draft class. Their careers prove that a team can find franchise quarterbacks without spending a premium first-round pick. This trend suggests that smart roster building relies more on player development than draft capital. Teams that can identify and coach up these middle-round gems gain a massive advantage in the salary cap era. The Cowboys have seen this firsthand with Howell backing up their star, while Brissett brings experience to the Arizona Cardinals. The data shows that the best QBs in the last 10 years were not the ones everyone expected to succeed. Sunday’s game at AT&T Stadium involves the middle-round underdogs.

item.title: Yan Diomande on Real Madrid: “I feel like we are a family”
item.description: Yan Diomande right winger of Real Madrid and Cote d'Ivoire during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Real Madrid at Spotify Camp Nou on October 25, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Real Madrid youngster Yan Diomande spoke about how the club is and acts like a family. Speaking to RM Play, he was asked about the atmosphere at the club, and how he is adjusting to life at Real Madrid — especially as a shy person. He said: “I am shy, I always have been, that has not changed. I am also the youngest in the squad. There are lots of fun and friendly players here… Vini, Kylian, Aurélien. I feel like we are a family.” Diomande also spoke about how it feels to actually play for Real Madrid at this age, and how things were so different just a few years ago when he used to watch this team on the television. He said: “It’s a pleasure, an honor to play with the best players in the world. I used to watch them on TV and now I share the same dressing room as them.” He also talked about his sister, and how he is able to work hard because of her, and dedicate everything to her and his mom. He said: “I think about my sister and mom, but especially my sister because, as everyone knows, I lost my sister. I give it my all every match in memory of my sister.”

item.title: Esteban Ocon’s F1 career could be over after shock early axe by Haas in Mexico
item.description: Esteban Ocon could have raced in Formula 1 for the last time after being axed by Haas for reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Ocon’s contract with Haas expires at the end of the year and he will be replaced by Brazilian driver and current F2 championship leader Rafael Camara for the 2027 season. However, Ocon, who won the 2021 Hungarian GP with Alpine, was expected to complete the rest of the 2026 campaign alongside Ollie Bearman . Ryo Hirakawa will race for Haas in Mexico this weekend (Reuters) Yet after appearing in second practice on Friday and getting embroiled in a row over tyres with race engineer Laura Muller, Haas released a statement on Saturday confirming that 31-year-old Japanese driver Hirakawa will take Ocon’s place for the rest of the weekend. Haas did not reveal the specific reason for the change, but did acknowledge that Ocon wasn’t ill. Haas team members were busy at work on Saturday morning removing Ocon’s name and number from their hospitality unit. When asked about the situation by Sky Sports F1 on Saturday, team principal Ayao Komatsu insisted he “could not go into details.” There are four races remaining after Mexico, starting with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in Brazil next week. It has not yet been confirmed whether it will be Ocon, Hirakawa, Camara or even another reserve in Jack Doohan, who’ll take to the track at Interlagos. Ocon, 30, is adamant that he does not think this year marks the end of his Formula 1 career, but his options are minimal for 2027. Only Racing Bulls and Cadillac have not confirmed their roster for next year, but neither team are thought to be interested in the Frenchman. Hirakawa, meanwhile, is a two-time winner of the World Endurance Championship with Toyota, who are Haas’ title sponsor and technical partner. He appeared in FP1 in a planned outing earlier on Friday.

item.title: 🤕 Bayern suffer double injury blow minutes apart against Dortmund
item.description: 🤕 Bayern suffer double injury blow minutes apart against Dortmund Bayern Munich hosts rivals Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, and things implode at the Allianz Arena within minutes. First, Ismael Saibari was forced off with an apparent ankle injury and was forced down the tunnel immediately after failing to continue. Then, just two minutes later, the hosts brought on a second player when Serge Gnabry went down, grabbing his lower leg. Nathaniel Brown and Josip Stanišić replaced the duo, respectively. Bayern then thought it got even worse in the first half as Jobe Bellingham stabbed the ball home for what he thought was his first Bundesliga goal. VAR, however, rightfully overturned the effort. In the blink of an eye, the hosts then struck on the break after a poor pass from Dortmund and Konrad Laimer broke the deadlock.

item.title: CIAC girls cross country championships: Brining, Lyme-Old Lyme take Class S crowns
item.description: Runners in Class S girls race take to the course during the CIAC Girls Cross Country Championships on Saturday, October 31, 2026 at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) Six CIAC girls cross country teams and runners will be crowned champions on Saturday at Wickham Park in Manchester. Here's the rundown. Brining, Lyme-Old Lyme take Class S girls crowns Hale-Ray freshman Ashley Brining has had plenty of experience running at Wickham Park entering the Class S girls race, despite being in her first year of high school. "I know that I'm a really good runner," Brining said. "I won states in seventh grade, and I was a really good runner in eighth grade, too, so I knew that I could do it." Brining holds the middle school record at Wickham Park, and her goal Saturday was to win the Class S championship. She did just that in 19:19.3. It wasn't a personal best, but the goal was a victory. "I try really hard, and I work really hard, and I have some really big goals, so I'm really trying to work as hard as I can and put everything into it," said Brining, who was already thinking about future races like the New England championship, which follows the State Open. In another big-time team battle, Lyme-Old Lyme defeated Shepaug, 49-51. In terms of team scoring, the Wildcats finished second, third, eighth, 14th and 22nd on the way to the first state championship in program history. The Spartans were first, ninth, 10th, 12th and 19th. Full results Oxford's DeLuise wins Class SS individual crown Junior Callie DeLuise of Oxford was running in second early in the race, but took over the lead just after the halfway point and cruised to a win in the Class SS race, finishing first with a personal-best time of 18:49.1. Rebecca Langlais of Tolland was second in 19:04.5. "Rebecca and I were going back and forth and switching positions, and after the green monster, I fell back a bit," DeLuise said. "Suddenly, I felt really good and I decided to just kick to the end and see how I could do." Senior Charlotte Behnke of Haddam-Killingworth finished third at 19.37.6, and sophomore Alyssa Behnke of Haddam-Killingworth came in fourth at 20:14.0. Full results Wasiolek, Mercy run to Class M crowns Mercy junior Cora Wasiolek ran to a victory in the Class M race with a time of 18:58.6, ahead of second-place finisher Edith Edie Ranta of RHAM, who came in at 19:12.5. "In the beginning, I just wanted to stay up with the leaders, and when it felt right, I decided to go," Wasiolek said. "Going down to the woods is where I made my first burst, right after mile one. Then I just wanted to keep it the rest of the way." Harper Vanacore of Sheehan was third at 19:50.1 and Charlotte Kenney of Branford came in fourth at 19:57.8. Mercy won the team title with a score of 26, well ahead of second-place Hand, which came in with 106. Mercy had Alyson Low (20:02.1) in fifth and Addison Akier (20:04.1) in sixth. item.title: Football Daily | Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream while Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. item.content:encoded: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
